page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. Built on the ARMv9 arm64 architecture, this server features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with one thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 7392.56 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 459.25 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in database operations, achieving 133.11 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 121.97 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

The instance offers high resource density for multi-threaded workloads, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for applications that can leverage parallel processing on ARM architecture. The inclusion of 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage reduces the need for external block storage, optimizing data-intensive workloads. However, the 2.0 GB of memory per core represents a tradeoff for memory-bound tasks. This server is appropriate for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression.
